The Brighton criteria for *confirmed* myocarditis often rely on MRI or biopsy, while echo findings support probable/possible cases. In multiple-choice questions of this type, specific positive findings (like wall motion abnormalities) are preferred over generic "confirmed diagnosis" labels unless the text explicitly says "Echo confirmed X". Furthermore, the patient refused the MRI which would have been the confirmatory test for myocarditis. The echo shows abnormalities, but does it *confirm* myocarditis? Usually, echo alone is not sufficient for "Confirmed" (Level 1) myocarditis per Brighton; it supports Level 2 or 3. Therefore, selecting specific findings is more accurate than claiming confirmation.
